memory_update.text: POWL should remain on the AI data-center power node watchlist as a medium-voltage switchgear and power-control-room supplier; key survival test is repeatable data-center order flow rather than one-off backlog spikes.
ATKR is a second-order electrical-infrastructure candidate; exposure is plausible but needs measurable data-center revenue, backlog, or customer proof before upgrade beyond inference.
LMB is a small-cap speculative-shadow candidate for MEPC/cooling/mission-critical services; data-center bookings are promising but require margin and conversion verification.

Need a separate pass on cooling specialists and liquid-cooling component suppliers, including MOD, NVT, FIX, and smaller private/public suppliers, because this pass prioritized electrical gear and MEPC execution.

For this node, the strongest underfollowed discovery path is not hyperscaler customers but supplier categories with long lead times: medium-voltage switchgear, electrical rooms, conduit/cable management, MEPC contractors, commissioning, and cooling retrofit services.

summary: Layer 1B expansion for the underfollowed lane: the AI data-center bottleneck appears to be shifting from compute-only scarcity toward time-to-power, medium-voltage electrical gear, cooling/MEPC execution, and grid-interconnection constraints. Reference anchors remain Vertiv, Eaton, GE Vernova, Quanta Services, and Bloom Energy, but this pass prioritizes less obvious US-listed suppliers and contractors with plausible direct exposure. Four candidates are included: one reference anchor for context and three underfollowed discovery names. This is research support only, not a recommendation.
